source.title: The Slingshot Mechanism: An Empirical Study of Adaptive Optimizers and the Grokking Phenomenon
source.authors: Vimal Thilak; Etai Littwin; Shuang-Fei Zhai; O. Saremi; Roni Paiss; J. Susskind

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendix in full; some plotted values are not stated numerically in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers and reports held-out generalization outcomes, using grokking and image-classification settings rather than the benchmarks and tuning protocol in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper tests optimizer choice against held-out accuracy, but does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolution versus fully connected networks, large-batch effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Training-only norm and loss plots are not rows for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The modular-division experiment compares held-out generalization with Adam versus momentum SGD, bearing on V4 in a new algorithmic setting. Adam generalizes while SGD does not at any of three tested learning rates, despite receiving three times as many updates. AdamW-only image results do not establish an optimizer ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase broadly captures the conclusion: adaptive optimizers exhibit late cyclic instabilities associated with grokking and often improved generalization. The authors present this as an empirical association and an implicit bias requiring explanation. Norm constraints can achieve comparable generalization without clear Slingshots, but stability needs qualification: Appendix C.1 explicitly reports persistent instability with weight decay, and normalization can also become unstable depending on temperature and task.
record.recipe_differences: Uses late-stage optimizer behavior and grokking datasets, rather than comparing optimizer held-out performance under the image and language benchmark tuning protocol described in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice; Adam epsilon; weight decay; learning rate; training dataset and split; normalization temperature. The authors report that Slingshot and generalization behavior vary with these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: With AdamW on full CIFAR-10, the best test accuracy occurs late, after a Slingshot; there is no SGD held-out comparator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late adaptive-optimizer training can improve image-classification accuracy, with peaks associated with Slingshot phases.

fits_no_version.finding: Algorithmic and synthetic experiments associate generalization with Slingshot phases and show sensitivity to Adam epsilon and other hyperparameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slingshot-associated generalization during prolonged adaptive optimization depends on the task and optimizer configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay and feature/parameter normalization can yield high validation accuracy without clear Slingshot cycles; stability depends on the configuration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Controlling norm growth can enable generalization without the usual Slingshot dynamics.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison is not a broad benchmark sweep and uses a specific algorithmic task and training recipe. The SGD result is explicitly limited to this setup. Several reported test or validation outcomes appear only in plots without numerical values; no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Training loss, training accuracy, weight-norm dynamics, feature changes, and curvature measurements were omitted because they do not measure a V1–V8 outcome. The optimizer comparison on a six-layer deep linear model reports training metrics only (Appendix A.0.5; Figure 11). The CIFAR-10 subset ViT runs report no expected generalization for the 1000-sample setup (Appendix A.0.1; Figure 7).

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Held-out performance comparisons between convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.

Adaptive-versus-SGD rankings on image and language benchmarks under the specified limited tuning; broader comparative tuning; recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching optimizers; word-level language modeling. The weight-decay experiments do not compare optimizer rankings.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects, including joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness ranking generalization gaps against norm and margin measures. Update-direction curvature is a different measure.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The AdamW-only CIFAR-10 result warrants no V4 verdict. The modular-division reversal limits extension to a new setting; it does not contradict V4's qualified claim about frequent outcomes on image and language benchmarks. Validation-loss double descent over training time does not test V2's width-dependent claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on images.
Image-classification and language benchmark tuning protocol; comparison under broader tuning; decoupled weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: Transformer described in Appendix B
rows.size_stated: 2 decoder layers, width 128, 4 attention heads; approximately 450K trainable parameters
rows.operation_detail: Trained on modular division data with Adam; validation accuracy improved during training.
rows.value: Validation accuracy starts improving after 10 steps; grokking is observed.
rows.note: The paper reports qualitative validation improvement and grokking; it does not give a numerical accuracy here.
rows.check: Read jointly with R2: Adam generalizes better than momentum SGD, reversing the adaptive-method disadvantage. The reported onset is approximately 10^5 steps, not 10 steps; the exponent was separated during text extraction. Appendix B.2 identifies 500,000 updates for the Adam/AdamW runs.

rows.subject: Transformer described in Appendix B
rows.size_stated: 2 decoder layers, width 128, 4 attention heads; approximately 450K trainable parameters
rows.operation_detail: Trained on modular division data for 1,500,000 steps with SGD and momentum.
rows.baseline: Adam/AdamW in the corresponding setup, described as showing grokking and generalization
rows.value: No evidence of grokking or generalization with this setup.
rows.note: The authors explicitly report no generalization with SGD in this setting; this does not establish a general optimizer ranking.
rows.check: The state is correct relative to V4: momentum SGD fails to generalize while Adam does. This covers learning rates 0.001, 0.01 and 0.1, momentum 0.9, and 1,500,000 updates; it does not establish a ranking under matched tuning or compute.

rows.subject: ViT model on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the full CIFAR-10 training set; the text reports test accuracy peaking after a Slingshot phase.

conditions.value: linear learning rate warmup for 1 epoch

rows.note: The text says test accuracy peaks in epochs following a Slingshot and that the maximum occurs very late; it does not state the accuracy numerically.
rows.check: AdamW test accuracy peaking after a Slingshot does not measure performance relative to SGD. Neither a partial V4 effect nor support for V4 follows from this row.

relationships.condition: Two-layer Transformer on modular division with the tested Adam and momentum-SGD recipes
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show Adam generalizing while momentum SGD does not across three learning rates despite three times as many updates, qualifying extension of the adaptive-method disadvantage to this algorithmic setting.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly generalized while momentum SGD failed despite more updates across tested learning rates, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
